label: Diesel Price — Trend vs. March Peak
change: A third major September hike, effective 6am Sept 22 (diesel +₱8.82/L, gasoline +₱4.88/L, kerosene +₱6.47/L), pushed pump prices past ₱100/L nationally — national average ~₱102.78/L diesel and ~₱90.35/L gasoline as of Sept 23 (Metro Manila averages ran slightly higher at ~₱105.90/L diesel). It follows the Sept 15 hike (diesel +₱4.31/L, gasoline +₱5.68/L) that had reversed a brief Sept 13 easing to ₱92.06/L, and the Sept 8 hike (diesel +₱5.18/L, gasoline +₱4.69/L) before that. All three are driven by continued Middle East conflict — most recently drone-attack damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline — curbing global crude/product supply, plus peso depreciation; transport groups renewed protests and Congress continued discussing a temporary fuel excise-tax suspension. Three-week cumulative increase now ₱18.31/L diesel, ₱15.25/L gasoline
source: DOE Fuel Price Watch / Zigwheels, Sept 23, 2026

label: VisMin Wholesale Electricity Spot Price (WESM)
change: Visayas August average was ₱18.59/kWh (+64.9% MoM from ₱11.29/kWh in July); Mindanao ₱19.56/kWh (+88.2% MoM from ₱10.39/kWh). On Sept 10, ERC ordered a regional Secondary Price Cap (computed per-region instead of system-wide) that simulations show would cut the August average to ₱8.47/kWh in Visayas (-54%) and ₱8.69/kWh in Mindanao (-56%); IEMOP is recalculating August settlements with revised utility bills due Sept 20, and DOE publicly endorsed the cap Sept 18. PEMC's market surveillance committee has opened a 60-day probe into generator bidding behavior around the price spikes
source: WESM data via BusinessMirror / Philstar / ERC, Sept 18, 2026
